keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Algerian row starts in 1963 although independence is dated 5 July 1962 (infobox); for 1962 it draws Algeria inside the French Fifth Republic shape, which the French dossier must correct.

2,323,477 km2 against the infobox's 2,381,741 km2 (no year), ratio 0.98. The Sand War infobox reads 'No territorial changes': Morocco took the posts of Hassi Beida and Tindjoub (Algeria retook them on 8 October, Morocco again in the week of 14 October) but the infobox records no change after OAU mediation, so the shape stands for 1963-75. region.text: Algeria, 'ending 132 years of French colonial rule'

ledger.note: 1962-07-05: Algeria becomes independent. 'Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962, ending 132 years of French colonial rule', after the war that began with the FLN attacks of 31 October-1 November 1954, the Evian Accords of March 1962 and a referendum in which Algerians 'overwhelmingly voted for independence'. Ben Bella took power in September 1962.

region.text: the Algerian posts of Hassi Beida and Tindjoub and the oasis of Tindouf, with Béchar: Morocco 'abandoned its attempts to control Béchar and Tindouf after OAU mediation'

ledger.note: 1963-09: the Sand War with Morocco begins. 'Full-blown confrontation began on September 25, 1963'; Morocco 'succeeded in taking the two border posts of Hassi Beida and Tindjoub' and launched an offensive on Tindouf on 13 October. The page does not date the seizure of the posts (Algeria retook them on 8 October and lost them again in the week of 14 October); the region is the provinces Morocco claimed, not the ground it held.

region.text: the Algerian posts of Hassi Beida and Tindjoub and the oasis of Tindouf, with Béchar: Morocco 'abandoned its attempts to control Béchar and Tindouf after OAU mediation'

ledger.note: 1963-11-04: the fighting ends. A ceasefire was declared on 30 October (in force 2 November) after Hassan and Ben Bella met in Bamako on 29 October; 'A Malian officer arrived on November 4 and enforced the Bamako Accord, ending the hostilities'. The OAU-mediated formal peace treaty followed on 20 February 1964. Result: 'Military stalemate', no territorial change.

wars.name: Algerian War
wars.outcome: Independence on 5 July 1962 (the ledger's founding event); the infobox gives the war as 1 November 1954 - 19 March 1962 and the Evian Accords as signed in March 1962.
wars.note: Fought before the state's life and under the French Fourth and Fifth Republics; the page gives no front line. The war itself belongs to the French dossiers; listed so that the reviewer can see it was considered.

wars.name: Sand War

zones.text: the Algerian posts of Hassi Beida and Tindjoub and the oasis of Tindouf, with Béchar: Morocco 'abandoned its attempts to control Béchar and Tindouf after OAU mediation'

wars.outcome: Military stalemate. Fighting 25 September-30 October 1963 round Hassi Beida, Tindjoub, Tindouf and Figuig; ceasefire enforced 4 November; OAU peace treaty 20 February 1964; Morocco 'abandoned all claims to Algerian territory in 1972 with the Accord of Ifrane' (ratified only in 1989 on the page). No territorial change.
wars.note: The page's infobox ends the war on 20 February 1964; the ledger closes the contest on 4 November 1963, when the hostilities ended.

wars.name: Algerian Civil War
wars.outcome: After 'the authorities intervened on 11 January 1992, cancelling the elections' the country 'descended into a bloody civil war from 1992 to 2002' (over 100,000 dead); the Armed Islamic Group declared a ceasefire in October 1997 and an amnesty under the Civil Concord ran to 13 January 2000. No border change.
wars.note: The page names no ground held by the insurgents, so no rebel dossier or contest zone is recorded.

certainty.note: Frontiers inherited from French Algeria. The Moroccan frontier was claimed by Morocco until the 1972 Accord of Ifrane (the page says Morocco ratified it only in 1989), and the pages opened give no treaty or survey for the Saharan frontiers with Mali, Niger, Libya and Mauritania; the level rests on the era, not on dated lines for those.

notes: Algeria: Cliopatria row "People's Democratic Republic of Algeria" 1963..2024 (three shapes), reviewed with two pages (budget 1-2). (1) The state is dated from independence on 5 July 1962; the 1962 keyframe is new, and French Fifth Republic's 1961-2023 shape still holds Algeria (known problem, eu-22): the French dossier must give up Algeria in 1962. (2) The Algeria page gives no boundary treaty or agreement for any frontier and no involvement in the Western Sahara conflict, and no adoption date for the name; none was opened further (budget). The Western Sahara war (1975-91) is not recorded here for that reason; the Morocco/Mauritania dossiers carry it. (3) The Sand War page has Morocco ratifying the 1972 accord only in 1989 (the page's date, not cross-checked). (4) The Sand War zone is the two Algerian wilayas of Tindouf and Bechar, a generous reading of the posts actually fought over. (5) No ruler list on the pages opened (Ben Bella September 1962, overthrown 1965 by Boumediene, Bouteflika resigned 2 April 2019, Tebboune from December 2019 are the only reigns dated); identity.rulers omitted. (6) No gazetteer names were needed.
